issues.legal_issue: The bar on a second revision does not prevent the High Court from using its inherent or supervisory powers to correct a grave failure of justice or abuse of process.
material_facts: After a police investigation produced a charge-sheet alleging offences, the Magistrate discharged the accused.
The complainant’s revision was dismissed by the Sessions Court.
The High Court allowed a further challenge, set aside the discharge order, and directed the Magistrate to consider the matter on its merits.
The Supreme Court upheld the High Court’s intervention but did not decide the merits of the alleged offences.
issues.conclusion: Although the further revision under Section 397 was barred, the High Court could use its inherent power and continuing supervisory jurisdiction to intervene where necessary to prevent miscarriage of justice or abuse of process; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 397(1) and 397(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure provide revisional powers and bar a further revision by the same person after one revisional forum has been approached. That bar does not extinguish the High Court’s inherent power under Section 482 or its supervisory jurisdiction under Section 483, and its suo motu revisional power under Section 401 remains available. The High Court should exercise these powers sparingly and cautiously to prevent grave miscarriage of justice, abuse of process, failure to follow required procedure, or correction-worthy illegality or error. This approach follows Madhu Limaye v. State of Maharashtra and V.C. Shukla v. State through C.B.I.; the broader observations in Dharampal and Rajan Kumar Manchanda do not bar inherent intervention in such circumstances. Deepti and Simrikhia were distinguished on their facts.

rule.if: criminal_proceeding and prior_session_revision and (grave_miscarriage_of_justice or abuse_of_process or required_procedure_not_followed or materially_incorrect_lower_court_order)

predicates.criminal_proceeding: The matter concerns a challenge to an order made in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.prior_session_revision: A party has already sought revision before the Sessions Court.
predicates.grave_miscarriage_of_justice: The lower-court process or order has caused, or would cause, a grave failure of justice.
predicates.abuse_of_process: The lower-court process is being abused.
predicates.required_procedure_not_followed: A required procedural step has not been followed in the lower-court proceeding.
predicates.materially_incorrect_lower_court_order: The lower-court order contains an error or illegality that calls for correction.

issues.definition: When a criminal matter has already been revised by the Sessions Court, the High Court may nevertheless intervene if a grave failure of justice, abuse of process, procedural failure, or materially incorrect lower-court order is present.

issues.legal_issue: The State is not treated as a person barred from seeking High Court revision by the restriction on a second revision.
material_facts: The judgment considered whether the restriction on a further revision applied when the State sought revisional relief.
The judgment described the State as the prosecutor responsible for conducting prosecutions on behalf of society and taking appropriate remedial steps.
issues.conclusion: The State is not prohibited by the restriction on a second revision from invoking the High Court’s revisional power.
issues.legal_principle: Section 397(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure bars a further revision by the same person after that person has approached either the High Court or the Sessions Judge. Applying the meaning of “person” in Section 11 of the Indian Penal Code, the Court held that the State is excluded by implication for this purpose because it prosecutes offenders on behalf of society and may take appropriate remedial steps; the State may therefore seek revision under Sections 397(1) and 401 of the Code.

predicates.criminal_proceeding: The matter concerns a challenge to an order made in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.state_is_prosecuting_offender: The State is conducting the prosecution of an alleged offender on behalf of society.
predicates.state_seeks_high_court_revision: The State seeks revisional relief from the High Court.

issues.definition: When the State prosecutes an alleged offender on behalf of society and seeks High Court revision in a criminal matter, it may seek that relief despite the restriction on a further revision.
